title: ARC Prize feedback sheet
scope: Two official-site asks, framed as an offer. Third-party resources lead; Mark’s own guides are offered for official hosting, with a link as the fallback.
context_from_mark: Matt—ARC Explainer is a hobby project I build in my own time, unpaid. I built these tools because I wanted to understand ARC and couldn’t find them anywhere. Thanks for already listing the Puzzle Explorer in your Tools section.
offer: This isn’t about traffic to my site. I’d happily shut it down if these things lived on arcprize.org. Anything I wrote is yours to copy, rehost or adapt; the code is public at https://github.com/82deutschmark/arc-explainer under the MIT license. If hosting something officially isn’t possible, a link works, and I’m glad to help in whatever way is useful.

asks.ask: Add missing ARC-3 community resources to the Resources catalogue, and host the public-game guides on arcprize.org behind a spoiler label.

community_resources.name: Red Pill/Blue Pill — interactive ARC game archive
community_resources.note: 252 community-made games. Playable copy, credited to the original: https://arc.markbarney.net/arc3/gallery?category=redbluepill

community_resources.name: Simon Ouellette — ARC-AGI-3 Training Data
community_resources.note: Separate from ARC_gym, which is already listed.

community_resources.name: Son Pham — ARC-3 games and agent harness
Symbolica — ARC-3 agents repository
community_resources.note: The existing Arcgentica entry is their ARC-2 write-up; this is the ARC-3 code.

asks.community_change: Add resource cards with direct links, a short description and creator credit.

game_guides.change: Host the guides on arcprize.org behind a spoiler label, next to each game. Fallback: a spoiler-labeled link from each official game page.

additional_resources.name: H-ARC: human solving data and visualizations

already_listed: Simon Strandgaard ARC-Interactive, arc-dataset-collection and arc-notes
asks.check: Each added card has a direct working destination, purpose and creator credit. Avoid duplicating existing catalogue entries.

asks.ask: Open the actual attempt from ARC1/2 result rows; show released reasoning, submitted/expected grids, mismatches and cost/time together. Add failed-task filters and same-task model comparisons when both records exist.
asks.why_it_is_feasible: ARC Prize already holds these records from its own testing, so this does not depend on Hugging Face or a third-party viewer.

examples.note: A failed Opus 4.6 attempt: reasoning, both predicted grids beside the expected ones, mismatch toggle.

asks.check: A reader can follow a result to its actual attempt. Source/settings are visible and unavailable fields are labeled.

open_questions: I asked a while back why raw results stopped appearing on Hugging Face and was told I’d hear back; I haven’t yet. If publication has ended, a quick confirmation would help, and it would make ask 2 the main way people can see how newer models reach their answers. I’d also love to know whether Opus 5.5’s ARC-3 results will be published; its results page currently shows dashes there.
